title: Reconciling Visual Perception and Generation in Diffusion Models
claim: One model can unify perception and generation by passing semantics and distributional knowledge between a discriminative branch and a diffusion branch.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, dashed top banner linking both panels
description: A wide two-panel diagram with hatched gray backgrounds, labeled a) on the left and b) on the right. A dashed line with a boxed label, 'Distributional Knowledge Transfer', runs across the top and joins the two panels. In panel a), a dog photo passes through a 'Noise Free' box, a gray cube, and a single-step blue bowtie U-Net marked '× 1 Step'. A purple semantic cube then feeds an orange classifier block. That block outputs class probabilities (Border Collie 0.78, Bulldog 0.32, Dachshund 0.26), and a red double arrow links these to a bell-curve distribution icon. In panel b), a dashed 'Semantic Driven' arrow carries a dashed purple cube into a '× T Step' diffusion U-Net. Gaussian noise enters the same U-Net, and an 'Add Noise' box links the noise to the original dog image. The U-Net outputs a distribution icon and a generated dog image. Red double arrows mark the supervision between the outputs and the real image.
caption: Unified image Understanding and synthesis within diffusion models: a) semantic driven image generation; b) distributional knowledge transfer from diffusion models for visual perception.
abstract: We present \textsc{GenRep}, a unified image understanding and synthesis model that jointly conducts discriminative learning and generative modeling in one training session. By leveraging Monte Carlo approximation, \textsc{GenRep} distills distributional knowledge embedded in diffusion models to guide the discriminative learning for visual perception tasks. Simultaneously, a semantic-driven image generation process is established, where high-level semantics learned from perception tasks can be used to inform image synthesis, creating a positive feedback loop for mutual boosts. Moreover, to reconcile the learning process for both tasks, a gradient alignment strategy is proposed to symmetrically modify the optimization directions of perception and generation losses. These designs empower \textsc{GenRep} to be a versatile and powerful model that achieves top-leading performance on both image understanding and generation benchmarks.
